ratings_why.fun: One verb, the duel, reads the same on the board, in the shop and in the fight, and watching a crowned champion swell on an empty lek is a clear thing to draft towards.
ratings_why.distinct: Comparing size and taking a quarter, losing on purpose to buy the shop winner, and empty slots as the stage play unlike any of today's tribes, though 'feed your biggest unit' is a familiar backbone.

verdict_why: The v2 rules gaps are closed and every card now reads; what is left is wording polish, so more rounds would make it different, not better.

points.text: Cantor of the Whetting Song is now correct but reads like a rules note. Move the repeat-and-stop-check detail into the Duel keyword's glossary so the card can just say 'Your duels happen twice.'
Lord of the Old Lek holds two unrelated effects in one box. Lead with the doubling, the fantasy, and put the damage line on its own line so a player sees both.
Sir Brennbart's 'Your shop duels:' prefix is awkward. Something like 'A shop unit that loses a duel to your unit costs 1 less this turn' reads at a glance.

The champion can change several times in one turn, and seven cards say 'champion' or 'biggest'. The crown on the board, with a duel preview showing who wins and what moves, is what makes the tribe readable; treat it as part of the design.
Sir Hartmut's deafness now shows in play, which lands the seed well. A small cork-pop and whetting cue on his free first loss would sell it on screen.

standouts.why: Dame Reisig judging the duel and then you buying the winner is the hens' choice in card form, and the losing-on-purpose play reads at once.
Prior of the Needle Refectory makes 'the stage to themselves' literal: empty slots next to the champion, plain to see on the board.
Grand Master Ottokar reads in one breath and is the order's never-beaten elder: duel everyone smaller, stop at the first you'd lose.

weakest.why: The longest, most procedural text in the tribe; a player has to stop and parse it.
Grit Pit Elder's two separate four-a-turn counters are fiddly and its fantasy is thin next to the named knights.
Pennon-Bearer is clear but generic; nothing in what it does says pennon or squire.

flags.note: Empty slots counting as survivors means a one-unit board always deals full damage on a win; worth the owner's eye.
Pilgrim with Keeper and Cantor takes three quarters of every shop unit several times a turn, as the design itself flags.
